clue.text: Indian with a touch of the sun ?

definitions.text: Indian with a touch of the sun ?

parts.words: Indian with a touch of the sun ?
parts.note: an old term for a Native American, read as someone whose skin is red from sunburn

explanation.surface: A sunburnt traveller in India.
explanation.definitionFit: An old, now offensive term for a Native American, read playfully as sunburnt skin.

clue.text: Is this man indispensable as co-driver abroad ?

definitions.text: Is this man indispensable as co-driver abroad ?

parts.words: Is this man indispensable as co-driver abroad ?
parts.note: an indispensable assistant is a trusty helper on one side; abroad, where traffic keeps right, a co-driver sits on the other side

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a co-driver is essential on a foreign rally.
explanation.definitionFit: A right-hand man is an indispensable helper; in left-hand-drive countries the co-driver sits on that side.

clue.text: Bad blood about one article in the game

indicators.note: the jumbled blood goes about the other letters, enclosing them
bad blood here is blood in a bad, jumbled order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Bad blood about a piece of writing in a sporting contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bad' jumbles BLOOD into DBOLO; 'about' places IA inside it, after the D.
explanation.definitionFit: A juggling toy spun on a string between two sticks, and the game played with it.

clue.text: War-lord gets the range

definitions.meaning: Lord ..., British commander and Secretary of State for War in 1914
a kitchen range, a cooking stove

explanation.definitionFit: Lord Kitchener led Britain's war effort; a kitchener is also an old word for a kitchen cooking stove.

clue.text: None of it is good

parts.note: the proverb that having none of this is good: no tidings is good tidings

explanation.surface: A pessimist's verdict on everything.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'no news is good news'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidings or information, which the proverb says is best when absent.

clue.text: Plot wickedness, or torment

parts.note: a garden plot is a bed
wickedness is evil

explanation.surface: Someone choosing between scheming wickedly and tormenting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plot' looks like a verb meaning scheme; it is a flower bed.
explanation.definitionFit: To plague or harass someone is to torment them.

clue.text: Forger under trade union ban?

parts.note: a forger is one who forges metal; work under a union ban is said to be blacked, giving a blacked craftsman

explanation.surface: A counterfeiter whose union has blacklisted him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forger' suggests a counterfeiter, but means someone working at a forge; a trade union 'blacks' work it bans.
explanation.definitionFit: A metalworker who shapes iron at a forge.

clue.text: Doctor goes to sick baboon

parts.note: sick means ill

explanation.surface: A vet visits an ailing monkey.
explanation.definitionFit: A West African baboon related to the mandrill.

clue.text: Not evil, but 'madly unrestrained

indicators.note: madly arranged, the words not evil are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone not wicked but wildly out of control.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting with uncontrolled force, without restraint.

clue.text: City where police get clues, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word is spoken, a soundalike

parts.note: police leads are clues to follow

explanation.surface: A city where detectives pick up clues.
explanation.walkthrough: Leeds is a city in Yorkshire, northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: A large city in West Yorkshire.

clue.text: General conveyance

definitions.meaning: Ulysses S. ..., the American Civil War general
a legal transfer of property or rights

explanation.definitionFit: Ulysses Grant was a Union general; in law a transfer of property by deed is a conveyance.

clue.text: We get change of air-some find it boring

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a change of the word air means its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: We take a change of air, though some find the trip dull.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the clue's last word; 'get' and 'find it' are only joining words, and 'some' is taken literally.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tiresome and tedious is boring.

clue.text: Also your description of Red Riding Hood's " granny " ?

definitions.text: description of Red Riding Hood's " granny " ?

parts.note: also means too
thy is the old form of your

explanation.surface: A remark on the wolf disguised as Little Red Riding Hood's grandmother.
explanation.walkthrough: The wolf posing as granny has great big teeth ('all the better to eat you with').
explanation.definitionFit: Showing many prominent teeth, as the wolf in the fairy tale does.

clue.text: Pots with expertise but ends with a poor set

parts.note: expertise is skill

indicators.note: a poor version of the word set is a badly arranged one

explanation.surface: Someone skilled at making pots ends up with a shoddy set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' rearranges SET into ETS; 'but ends with a' merely joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Frying pans are cooking pots.

clue.text: Relish a dance ? What cheek !

parts.note: a caper is a playful skipping dance
sauce is cheek, impudence

explanation.surface: Someone enjoying a dance while being told off for impertinence.
explanation.definitionFit: A condiment made with pickled capers, served with mutton.

clue.text: Add lustre to a party with the Navy

parts.note: a do is a party
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A naval party brightens up the evening.
explanation.definitionFit: To decorate or embellish is to add lustre.

clue.text: Old university is to change round degrees

indicators.note: the word for change goes round the degrees, enclosing them

parts.note: to change is to alter
two MAs, Master of Arts degrees

explanation.surface: An old university plans to reorganise its degree courses.
explanation.walkthrough: Alma mater is Latin for 'nourishing mother'; 'is to' only joins, and the two degrees sit together inside the word for change.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin 'nourishing mother', the school or college one attended.

clue.text: Military ceremony Caesar was late for ?

definitions.text: Military ceremony Caesar was late for ?

parts.words: Military ceremony Caesar was late for ?
parts.note: a parade of troops; Caesar was warned of the Ides of a certain month and was killed when it had gone by

explanation.surface: Caesar arrives late for a parade.
explanation.walkthrough: Caesar told the soothsayer 'The Ides of March are come', who replied 'Ay, but not gone': he died after the Ides had arrived.
explanation.definitionFit: A parade in which troops walk by a saluting point; read also as the month having gone by.

clue.text: Scent has gone up dilute!

parts.note: rose is the past of rise, meaning went up
to water something is to dilute it

explanation.surface: Perfume prices have risen, so the stuff is being thinned.
explanation.definitionFit: A fragrant liquid distilled from petals, used as perfume.

clue.text: Submarine type off course

parts.note: a diver works under the sea, so is submarine
a gent is a chap or type of person

explanation.surface: A submarine of some class has strayed off its course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Submarine type' reads as one phrase meaning a kind of submarine, but it splits into two pieces: someone who works underwater, and a word for a chap.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving in different directions, deviating from a course.

clue.text: A number of narrow ways in depressed areas

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral five
alleys are narrow lanes

explanation.surface: Narrow streets in a run-down part of town.
explanation.definitionFit: Low-lying land between hills is literally depressed ground.

clue.text: Marie was one of those who suffered under the Commonwealth

definitions.text: Marie was one of those who suffered under the Commonwealth

parts.words: Marie was one of those who suffered under the Commonwealth
parts.note: Marie Lloyd sang 'One of the ... That Cromwell Knocked About a Bit'; Cromwell ruled during the Commonwealth

explanation.surface: A woman named Marie persecuted during Cromwell's rule.
explanation.walkthrough: Marie Lloyd was a British music-hall star; the Commonwealth was Cromwell's republic of the 1650s, whose troops wrecked many castles.
explanation.definitionFit: Castles battered by Cromwell's forces are remains of buildings, as the music-hall song says.

clue.text: India and spring together stay in the mind

parts.note: a well is a spring of water

explanation.surface: India and its springs linger in the memory.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwell within, as a thought abides in a person.

clue.text: Swimmer has won Olympic title?

parts.note: a swimmer that has taken gold, read as a creature both golden and aquatic

explanation.surface: An Olympic swimmer wins a gold medal.
explanation.definitionFit: An orange-gold ornamental carp is a pond swimmer coloured like a winner's medal.

clue.text: Easy catch, this shellfish

definitions.meaning: a simple chance in cricket, a dolly

explanation.definitionFit: A cricket catch that is a gift; also a clam with a gaping shell.

clue.text: Tuck, Bacon perhaps

definitions.meaning: Robin Hood's portly companion, a cleric
Roger Bacon, the thirteenth-century Franciscan scholar

explanation.definitionFit: Both Tuck of the Robin Hood legend and Roger Bacon were members of religious orders.

clue.text: No light opponent: for a boxer

definitions.meaning: a dark area where light is blocked
a boxer training alone spars with an imaginary opponent

explanation.definitionFit: An area of darkness cast by an object; in shadow-boxing the imagined rival you spar with.

clue.text: Man has these lockers in the house

definitions.text: Man has these lockers in the house

parts.words: Man has these lockers in the house
parts.note: devices that lock; the Isle of Man's parliament has a lower chamber named after them

explanation.surface: A householder with locks fitted.
explanation.walkthrough: The House of Keys is the elected chamber of the Isle of Man's parliament, Tynwald.
explanation.definitionFit: Objects used to work locks, which also name the Manx lower house.

clue.text: Foreshadow grief-pure nonsense

indicators.note: making nonsense of the words grief and pure jumbles their letters

explanation.surface: An omen of grief, utter nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: To foreshadow is to represent or suggest beforehand.

clue.text: Expert on a small part of France

parts.note: dept is short for département, an administrative division of France

explanation.surface: An expert on a little region of France.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone highly skilled is an expert.

clue.text: Hold back after one fault?

definitions.meaning: in tennis a server who faults serves again

explanation.definitionFit: To keep in store; read as 're-serve', what a tennis player does after a first fault.

clue.text: Colonist who pays his way

definitions.meaning: someone who makes a home in a new land

explanation.definitionFit: A pioneer living in a new colony; also one who settles accounts.
